version.changelog: Release 1.0.5: the app link now points to the real Windows Multi-Tool Suite build (multitool.zip) with its SHA-256.

llm.summary: The scripts fit the suite’s purpose, but misleading assurances about Windows security and broad script-unblocking advice warrant review.

dimensions.detail: Workspace creation, local configuration, and optional provider keys fit the purpose. A user-specified workspace can be outside the profile, contradicting the absolute profile-only promise without establishing uncontrolled access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: FAQ lines 80–83 dismiss script risk because there is no binary. The install guide recommends wildcard unblocking and a recursive fallback. Scripts can trigger [Defender protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/amsi-on-mdav); the text-only reassurance is unsound, although the guide explicitly discourages Defender exclusions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Installation and workflow execution are user-directed. Skill installation targets three fixed names and has a documented skip option.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent changes are disclosed workspace files, installed skills, and a Start Menu shortcut. No elevation, startup execution, service, or scheduled worker appears in the bundled scripts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Setup installs three disclosed skills; the launcher runs explicitly selected workflows. The bundled code shows no trading, email sending, credential harvesting, or telemetry.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Verify each script before unblocking it, preserve Defender and workplace security policies, and review the three separately installed skills. The optional unsigned desktop app is outside this inspection; a matching publisher-supplied hash does not establish safety.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Downgraded: environment variables and command use are disclosed and purpose-aligned. Missing tool-scope metadata alone does not demonstrate excessive authority.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported as a guidance concern: reading scripts is encouraged, but blanket unblocking accompanies misleading safety assurances. [Microsoft documents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/unblock-file) that unblocking removes download-origin marking and advises verifying files and their source first.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded to a documentation mismatch: the custom destination is explicitly supplied by the user, and the guide even illustrates an outside-profile path. No automatic escape or privilege escalation is shown.
